selected.title: A record number of whale calves have died in Patagonia
selected.summary: More than 300 southern right whale calves have died since June; researchers detected a disease-causing bacterium in samples, but its role in the die-off remains unclear.
selected.why_it_matters: The episode raises questions about how infection, animal health and environmental conditions interact in a recovering whale population.
selected.challenge_question: What do scientists currently know about the Patagonia whale-calf die-off?
selected.answer_explanation: Researchers reported that samples tested positive for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, but the evidence does not yet establish that the bacterium explains the exceptional scale of deaths.
selected.butterfly_question: How might a changing ocean alter disease risks for wildlife—and the people and ecosystems connected to it?

selected.title: A tiny marine microbe is testing how small life can get
selected.summary: Researchers identified genetic material from a marine microbe inside plankton off Japan. Its highly reduced genome appears to depend on a host, and the organism has not yet been directly observed.
selected.why_it_matters: Understanding how cells rely on hosts could reshape research on microbial ecosystems and the boundary between cellular life and virus-like dependence.
selected.challenge_question: Where did researchers find the genetic material of the tiny microbe Sukunaarchaeum?
selected.answer_explanation: The researchers encountered the microbe's genetic material while studying single-celled plankton collected in surface seawater off Shimoda, Japan.
selected.butterfly_question: If some organisms can outsource essential functions to hosts, how does that change what counts as an independent living thing?

sources.title: Microbe Discovered With One of The Smallest Genomes on Record

selected.title: A century of recipes shows Britain's seafood repertoire narrowed
selected.summary: A study of a century of UK magazine recipes reports that seafood dishes increasingly centered on a small group of species, reflecting changes in supply and trade.
selected.why_it_matters: What appears on household menus can reveal how fisheries, imports and food culture shape each other over time.
selected.challenge_question: Which broad trend did researchers identify in a century of UK seafood recipes?
selected.answer_explanation: The reported study found that recipes narrowed toward a small set of commonly featured seafood species, linking food habits with changing supply and trade.
selected.butterfly_question: How do supply chains and changing fish populations quietly reshape what a country considers familiar food?

sources.title: 100-year magazine study reveals ‘narrowing’ of UK seafood recipes

selected.title: A new structure has been reported inside solar-wind turbulence
selected.summary: A University of Tokyo research summary describes a reversal in the rotation sense of turbulent magnetic fields over a particular wavelength in the solar wind.
selected.why_it_matters: Improved understanding of solar-wind turbulence can inform models of space environments that affect spacecraft and planetary systems.
selected.challenge_question: What did the reported solar-wind study identify over a certain wavelength?
selected.answer_explanation: The research summary describes a reversal in magnetic-field rotation sense over a certain wavelength within turbulent solar-wind fields.
selected.butterfly_question: How could better models of the turbulent solar wind improve our ability to protect spacecraft and understand planets?

sources.title: Structure in the unstructured: New phenomenon discovered in the solar wind

selected.title: Physicists report observing a long-predicted quantum energy pattern
selected.summary: A research team led by Caltech says it experimentally tested predictions about how systems near critical tipping points absorb energy, decades after the underlying theory was proposed.
selected.why_it_matters: Better ways to test universal behavior near critical points could help scientists compare seemingly different physical systems.
selected.challenge_question: What physical setting did the report say the team used to test the prediction?
selected.answer_explanation: The report describes a chain of strontium atoms used in the experiment. The result concerns a specific test of theoretical predictions, not a general practical technology breakthrough.
selected.butterfly_question: Could a pattern shared by different materials help us predict how complex systems behave near a tipping point?

sources.title: After 40 Years, Physicists Finally Observe The 'Energy Ladder' at Quantum Tipping Points
